screen: Task Management — task-core (Task Management Dashboard, My Tasks, Projects & Workstreams, Dependencies & Workstreams, Task Calendar, + 2 unrouted legacy files)
screenLevelGaps: CUSTOMER CLAIM 1 — 'custom task creation is missing' — WRONG, with evidence. create-task-modal.tsx:504-524 renders an explicit two-button segmented toggle `[['catalogue','From job role'],['custom','Custom task']]`. Choosing 'Custom task' swaps the catalogue combobox for a free-text `<input>` (L511) plus an 'Also save to the Job Role Task library' checkbox (L515) that POSTs the typed title into the Competency module's jobrole-tasks library via competencyLibrariesService.create(ctx,'jobrole-task',{task,jobrole,task_type}) (L300-312). The feature exists and is wired. What IS missing is that a custom task STILL requires the Department -> Job Role -> Assign To funnel (the 'Assign To' options come from `departmentEmployees`, L526, which is empty until a Department is chosen, L167-171), and the 'Job Role *' label carries a required asterisk (L499) although submit() never validates it (L315).

CUSTOMER CLAIM 2 — 'custom task creation is not wired into Projects & Workstreams' — CONFIRMED in the Projects direction, WRONG in the task direction. projects-list-view.tsx imports only CreateProjectModal (L16); CreateTaskModal is never imported or rendered anywhere in that file. The only header action is 'New Project' (L67) and the drawer's 'tasks' tab (L126-133) can only tick pre-existing tasks. There is no 'Add Task' affordance on the project board or in the project drawer at all. The REVERSE link does exist: create-task-modal.tsx:540-570 has a whole 'Project delivery' fieldset (Project / Workstream / Dependency type / Waits for / Lag) and submit() calls attachTaskToProject + createDependency via linkProjectAndDependencies (L267-292), backed by real routes POST /task-management/projects/{id}/tasks (routes/api.php:975) and POST /task-management/dependencies (routes/api.php:934).

CUSTOMER CLAIM 3 — 'the Dependencies view PROJECT FILTER does not work and is not properly connected to project creation and task linking' — CONFIRMED, in four independent ways. (a) dependencies-view.tsx:438-443 hardcodes the only two project filter options as the literal strings 'Alpha Release' and 'Beta Testing'; the real project list IS fetched (data.options.projects, DependencyController.php:52-53) but is used only inside the Create Dependency dialog, never in the Filters menu. (b) The filter predicate compares `node.data.project` (L288) against those strings, and node.data.project is the project NAME (DependencyController::taskNodes -> `p.name`), while the dialog's project Select uses `String(project.id)` (L714) — so even a correct wiring would compare ids to names. (c) getDependencies is called with no arguments (L237) so the server-side `project_id` filter that DependencyController::index:27 implements is never exercised. (d) The dialog's Project + Workstream selections are silently DISCARDED by the API: task_management_dependencies has no project_id or workstream_id column (2026_07_29_000000_create_task_management_dependency_tables.php:12-27) and DependencyController::payload (L269-275) writes only predecessor/successor/type/lag/notes/tenant.

Dependencies: the Filter By Assignee options are likewise hardcoded demo names — 'Sarah', 'Michael', 'Dwight' (L426,429,432) — while the real user list is fetched into data.options.users (DependencyController.php:56-58) and never rendered. Any real tenant sees three filters that match nobody.

Dependencies: predecessor/successor pickers (L718-719) list ALL 500 most-recent tenant tasks unfiltered by the chosen project, yet DependencyController::store rejects the pair unless they already share a project (shareProject(), L224-233). Users will repeatedly hit 'Dependencies require two tasks from the same project.' The backend even returns per-task project_id from taskOptions() (L206) but types/task-management.ts:319 omits project_id from the options.tasks shape, so the frontend cannot scope the list.

JOB-ROLE TASK -> COMPETENCY LINK IS STRING-ONLY AND ONE-WAY. A catalogue task is read from s_user_jobrole_task via GET /table_data?table=s_user_jobrole_task&filters[jobrole]=<role NAME> (services/task/index.ts:594-625). s_user_jobrole_task has columns sector/track/jobrole/critical_work_function/task/task_category and NO skill, competency or proficiency column (migration 2025_06_12_105118). When the task is created, only the TITLE STRING is copied — createLegacyTask (services/task/index.ts:483-523) never sends the catalogue row id, and the `task` table has no jobrole_task_id, jobrole or competency column (2025_06_21_050744_create_task_table.php). So once created, a job-role task is indistinguishable from a custom task and cannot be traced back to the job role or its competency framework.

THE ONLY COMPETENCY HOOK ON A TASK IS `task.skill_id`, AND IT IS OPTIONAL. 'Skills Required' (create-task-modal L529) is populated from GET /user-skills/{id}, which resolves tbluser.allocated_standards -> s_library_map(type='jobrole').skill_ids -> s_users_skills (UserSkillController.php:56-95) — i.e. the job role's mapped skill library, correctly Competency-owned. Those ids are written comma-joined into task.skill_id and task.required_skills (taskController.php:507-509,548-550). But the field is optional, no proficiency LEVEL is captured, and s_skill_matrix (the per-employee proficiency store) is never read to check the assignee actually holds the skill nor written on completion. Task Management therefore produces no competency evidence.

TASK -> LMS REMEDIATION EXISTS BUT IS INVISIBLE ON EVERY SCREEN IN THIS UNIT. Rejecting a completed task sets approve_status='Rejected' and status='ON HOLD' (WorkspaceController::approve L346-356). GET /user-rejected-tasks-courses (routes/api.php:853 -> SkillMatchingController::getCoursesForUserRejectedTasksSkills L201-268) maps task.approve_status='Rejected' -> task.skill_id -> sub_std_map.subject_id to recommend courses. taskService.getRejectedTaskLearning exists, but its ONLY consumer in the whole frontend is components/domain/task/tm-reports.tsx:58 — neither the Dashboard approvals board, My Tasks, nor the task drawer ever surfaces or triggers it. And it returns nothing unless the assigner happened to tick Skills Required.

NO EVENT MECHANISM. app/Events, app/Listeners and app/Observers do not exist, so nothing in Task Management can broadcast completion/approval to Competency, LMS or Talent. Every cross-module hand-off in this unit is either an explicit client-side sequential call (create task -> attachTaskToProject -> createDependency, create-task-modal L267-292) or absent.

PROJECT PERMISSION MISMATCH. ProjectController::index (L20-55) returns every non-archived project of the tenant, but Edit / Archive / Manage Team / Link Tasks / Workstreams all gate on canManage() = created_by OR manager_id OR sponsor_id (L403-408). A project TEAM MEMBER is not included. projects-list-view.tsx renders the Edit/Manage/Archive menu on every card unconditionally (L92), and create-task-modal offers every project in its Project select (L547-549), so ordinary users get 403s ('You cannot link tasks.') surfaced as 'The task was created, but linking it to the project failed'.

TWO OF THE TEN FILES ARE UNROUTED DEAD CODE. hooks/content-map-m6.ts:33-37 maps exactly five task components (TaskWorkspace, MyTasksView, ProjectsListView, DependenciesView, TaskCalendarView) to menuIds 210-214. task-approvals-view.tsx and task-details-drawer.tsx are exported from components/domain/task/index.ts (L8, L11) but rendered by nothing. task-approvals-view.tsx additionally hardcodes a fabricated task 'T-999 Update Q3 Financial Models / Oscar Martinez' (L23-39) and its Approve/Reject buttons are literal no-ops (L153,160).

The Task Management Dashboard KPI tiles (task-workspace.tsx:77-82) are the only KPI row in the module that is NOT clickable — My Tasks' four tiles each carry an `action` that re-filters the list (my-tasks-view.tsx:147,154,161,168). Four dead-end numbers on the module's landing screen.

Substantial backend surface has no UI in this unit: comments (POST /workspace/{id}/comments), time tracking (start/stop), subtasks, recurrence, attachment versions, activity feed, workload, milestone create/update/delete, dependency UPDATE, task templates, global search and the assignment-capacity check are all routed (routes/api.php:889-948) and several have service wrappers (addWorkspaceComment, getWorkspaceWorkload, updateWorkspaceTask, createMilestone, updateDependency, getEmployeeTaskSuggestions, getTaskDescription, getJobRoleEmployees) with ZERO callers anywhere in the frontend.

The Dashboard exposes no Priority, Assignee, Project or date-range filter although WorkspaceController::index validates and implements all four (L56-61,102-118) and returns priority_options in filters (L150).

'Subordinate Tasks' (my-tasks-view.tsx:66) is the only place in the module that consumes the HRIT reporting line (MyTasksController::applyGroup L296). Department, job role and hierarchy are otherwise read only as display strings; nothing in Task Management writes back to Organization/HRIT.
